The words

Lord, I am Thine, for Thou hast died for me;
Thy claim I own, and give myself to Thee;
Not with the price of gold, of gold most fine
Hast Thou redeemed my soul, and made me Thine.

Thy blood was shed upon the awful tree;
I marvel at the love there shown for me
All loveless, and to sin and self a slave; —
Thy gifts enriched me, yet I nothing gave.

Now in its wonder would my soul arise,
Shorn of all pride, but precious in Thine eyes,
Who for its life Thy glory laidst aside,
And wore its shame, and for its purchase died;

And fired with love, that wondrous love proclaim
In life, in death, in fealty to Thy name;
In loving service, for such service given,
Here upon earth, and yonder in Thy heaven.

Lord, I am Thine, Thy love hath won my soul;
Now shall my life obey such sweet control; —
No, not mine own, the purchase is complete,
I bring my all to lay it at Thy feet.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum Eb and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on m (G).
  • Count the time. 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l and the chromatic fe. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Morningland (Paisley, 1911).

The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Tens (10.10.10.10), and this page sets them to EVENTIDE; any other Tens tune fits them as well.

  • Words: Traditional Greek
  • Translated (1911): John Brownlie (1857–1925)
  • Melody (1861): William Henry Monk (1823–1889)

Tune EVENTIDE by William Henry Monk (1823–1889); words by Traditional Greek; translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925).

Sung to the same tune: Abide with Me, Father Divine, This Deadening Power Control, Lord, Let Our Eyes the Things Unseen Behold, Not Worthy, Lord, to Gather Up the Crumbs.

Questions about Lord, I Am Thine, for Thou Hast Died for Me

What is the doh of Lord, I Am Thine, for Thou Hast Died for Me?

In this version, in Eb major, doh is Eb. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Lord, I Am Thine, for Thou Hast Died for Me start on?

It starts on m (G in Eb major). Find doh first, then sing up or down to m.

Is Lord, I Am Thine, for Thou Hast Died for Me in the public domain?

Yes. John Brownlie died in 1925, William Henry Monk died in 1889; the words were in print by 1911 and the music in 1861. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
